frames.u: Test with a real offer, not a survey

reel1.caption:
"Great idea!" is not a customer. Compliments are free, so they prove very little.

The real signals: someone asks how much, someone books a date, someone pays a deposit. Make a small, real offer and see who says yes.

Send this to a friend who is starting out.

frames.b: What is left is your pay.

reel2.caption:
A sale is not profit. Before you launch, do the maths on one sale.

Write down the price, take off the direct costs like materials, fuel, data and fees, then see what is left for your time. Divide by the hours it takes. That is your real hourly pay.

slides.title: Separate account
slides.head: Business money in one place.
slides.body: Ask at least two banks about fees and documents. If you cannot open one yet, use a second account only for the business.

slides.title: Pay yourself
slides.head: A fixed amount on a fixed day.
slides.body: Act like an employee of your business. The rest stays in the business as a buffer.

slides.title: Use pots
slides.head: Operating, tax, buffer, growth.
slides.body: Move a share of each payment into tax. Ask an accountant what share is right for you.

slides.title: Keep records
slides.head: Photo every receipt and invoice.
slides.body: Log date, who, amount and category. Simple enough that you will actually do it.

slides.title: 15 minutes a week
slides.head: Check what came in and went out.
slides.body: Chase unpaid invoices and ask one question: did I make a profit this week?

slides.sub: Come back to it on payday.

carousel.caption:
When business and personal money sit in one pile, you never know if the business is making money.

Five steps: a separate account, a fixed pay day, simple pots for tax and buffer, easy records, and a 15 minute weekly check. Check current tax rules on sars.gov.za or ask an accountant.
